tips.title: Choosing the Right Cement for ABS vs Polystyrene
tips.text: Tamiya Extra Thin Cement bonds polystyrene perfectly by melting the plastic together, but it struggles with ABS parts found in many modern kits (breeches, gun barrels, ICM and Arma Hobby aircraft propellers). For ABS, switch to Tamiya ABS & Polystyrene Cement in the green bottle, which contains ABS-compatible solvents. Apply sparingly with a fine brush to both surfaces, press together for 10 seconds, and let cure for 24 hours before sanding. Test the bond on a spare sprue first.

tips.title: Selecting Paint Type: Acrylic vs Enamel vs Lacquer
tips.text: For most scale model applications, Vallejo's Model Air (acrylic) and Model Color (acrylic with additives) are recommended. Acrylics offer vibrant colors, ease of use, and quick drying times. For enamel effects or when using aged colors, consider AMMO by Mig Jimenez' Acrylic Paints (with built-in enamel effect). Lacquers like Tamiya's are less common but suitable for clear coats and metallics. Always test paints on a spare part before use.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits for Each Stage
tips.text: For plastic models, use wet-or-dry sandpaper from brands like Tamiya or Everbilt. Start with 400-600 grit for initial sanding of joins and seams, then progress to 800-1000 grit for smoothing and preparing surfaces for painting. Finally, use 1500-2000 grit for polishing and achieving a gloss finish before applying decals. Always sand in one direction and rinse parts with water after each grit.

tips.title: Filling Gaps: Tamiya Putty vs Vallejo Plastic Putty vs Super Glue + Baking Soda
tips.text: Tamiya's Liquid Putty and Vallejo's Plastic Putty are both versatile fillers for gaps and seams. Apply with a fine brush, let dry, then sand smooth with progressively finer grits. For deep gaps or undercarriage bay doors, mix super glue with a pinch of baking soda to create a gap-filling putty. Apply with a toothpick, let cure, then sand and clean with isopropyl alcohol.

tips.title: Decal Setting Solutions: Micro Set/Sol vs Mr. Mark Softer
tips.text: For setting decals, choose between Micro Scale's Micro Set (decalsolvent) and Micro Sol (wetter). Apply Micro Set to the decal, let it soak for 10-15 seconds, then apply Micro Sol to flatten and bond the decal. For harder-to-settle decals, consider Mr. Mark Softer, a stronger decal solvent. Always test setting solutions on a spare decal first to avoid damaging graphics.
